title: Quantum Key Distribution and Composable Secrecy

items.title: Finite authenticated key-distribution protocol
items.statement: A finite two-party key-distribution protocol has a finite nonempty key alphabet, a finite public transcript alphabet, finite-dimensional quantum registers, finitely many rounds of local quantum channels and measurements, and final classical outputs in the key alphabet or a common abort symbol. Its authenticated public messages are delivered unchanged to the other honest party and disclosed to the adversary. For each adversarial strategy its final normalized output is a classical-classical-classical-quantum state on Alice's key, Bob's key, transcript, and the adversary's retained quantum system.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014)
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015)
M. Ben-Or, M. Horodecki, D. W. Leung, D. Mayers, and J. Oppenheim, The Universal Composable Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2005)
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018)

items.title: The finite classical key-copy map is a quantum channel
items.statement: For a finite nonempty key alphabet K and finite-dimensional transcript and adversary registers, define C(X)=sum_k L_k X L_k^dagger from ATE to ABTE, where L_k=|k,k><k|_A tensor I_TE. Then C is completely positive and trace-preserving. On a state classical in A, C copies its basis label into B and leaves the transcript and adversary system unchanged.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §4.3
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), §§1.1.3 and 2.2.2

items.title: Trace norm of a finite classical block operator
items.statement: If X_i are self-adjoint endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space E indexed by a finite set I, and (|i>) is the computational basis of C^I, then ||sum_i |i><i| tensor X_i||_1=sum_i ||X_i||_1.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 1, §1.1.3
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §2.1

items.title: Abort-aware real and ideal QKD outputs and security errors
items.statement: For a fixed adversarial strategy, let p_acc be the acceptance probability and rho^top_ABTE the normalized real output conditioned on acceptance when p_acc>0. Define the ideal full output to retain the real abort branch and accepted transcript-adversary marginal, while replacing the accepted keys by a uniform shared key independent of transcript and adversary. Define epsilon_cor=Pr[accept and K_A != K_B], epsilon_sec=p_acc D(rho^top_ATE, tau_A tensor rho^top_TE), with epsilon_sec=0 if p_acc=0, and delta_real-ideal as the trace distance of the normalized full real and ideal states.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §§3.3–4.3
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3
M. Ben-Or, M. Horodecki, D. W. Leung, D. Mayers, and J. Oppenheim, The Universal Composable Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2005), §4
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 1, §1.1.3

items.title: Replacing Bob's key by a copy of Alice's costs the correctness error
items.statement: For a normalized finite classical-classical-classical-quantum state rho_ABTE with blocks R_E^{a,b,t}, define rho_ATE=sum_{a,t}|a,t><a,t| tensor sum_b R_E^{a,b,t} and gamma=C(rho_ATE), where C copies Alice's classical key into B. Then D(rho_ABTE,gamma)=Pr[K_A != K_B].

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §4.3, Theorem 4.1 proof
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 1, §1.1.3

items.title: The abort-aware ideal output and conditional marginals are states
items.statement: For every finite protocol output in the preceding definition, the conditional accepted real state and each transcript-adversary marginal used there are density operators when p_acc>0; the displayed abort-aware ideal full output is also a density operator. If p_acc=0, the ideal output equals the real abort-only state.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §4.2
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3

items.title: QKD composable secrecy is bounded by correctness plus secrecy
items.statement: For every finite authenticated key-distribution protocol and each adversarial strategy, the trace distance between the abort-aware real and ideal outputs is at most epsilon_cor+epsilon_sec. Consequently, uniform correctness and secrecy bounds over all strategies add to a uniform real-ideal bound.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), Theorem 4.1
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3, Proposition 8.3.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 1, §1.1.3

title: Quantum Key Distribution and Composable Secrecy — Examples

items.title: Abort probability weights an otherwise imperfect one-bit key
items.statement: Let a finite protocol abort with probability 1/4 and, when it accepts, output the shared key 0 with probability one, with trivial transcript and a one-dimensional adversary system. Its correctness error is 0, its secrecy error is 3/8, and its abort-aware real-ideal trace distance is exactly 3/8.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §4.3
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3

items.title: Secrecy and correctness are separate requirements
items.statement: For K={0,1} and no abort, the state with Alice's key uniform and independent of a trivial adversary but Bob's key always its complement has epsilon_sec=0, epsilon_cor=1, and real-ideal distance 1. Conversely, if both parties always output 0 and the adversary is trivial, then epsilon_cor=0 while epsilon_sec and real-ideal distance equal 1/2.

references.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), §4.3
Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), §8.3
